agree.reason: The opening quotes her own $600K figure and the break-even math is concrete, so a reply is likely, but the IT director's resistance only gets one line and could still stop it.

honest.reason: The halving is correctly tied to one customer and the 21% result is disclosed, but 'our other customer that tracks errors' hides that a third tracking customer hasn't shared numbers, which could be bad news.

works_the_facts.reason: The $75,000 a year for five sites, the 12.5% break-even against $600K, the 21% from 2.8 to 2.2 and the 'more than half' from 4.1 to 1.9 are all correctly derived and well chosen.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is her ongoing $600K-plus loss, which the break-even sets against the cost, though it never says outright that doing nothing keeps that cost every year.

qualification.reason: 'If return costs track mis-picks' names a real assumption she can check, but there is no date, no measurable target and no consequence if results fall short, such as a trial period or an exit clause.

objections.reason: Saying it 'sits on top' of the WMS with three-week setup partly meets the IT objection, but 'sits on top' doesn't spell out how little IT work or system integration is needed, which is what the director would want to know.

fit.reason: It is short and easy to read on a phone, with a pointed subject line and one clear ask.
